```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Restoring all automatic domestic cuts would deny WIC nutrition to 750,000 mothers and children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Restoring all automatic domestic cuts would eliminate Title I funding for 1.8 million low-income school children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Restoring all automatic domestic cuts would deny 734,000 households home heating assistance.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Restoring all automatic domestic cuts would cut financing of all federal regulatory agencies by 10%.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for reauthorizing federal funding of extended unemployment insurance.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"If federal funding of extended unemployment insurance is not reauthorized, 1.5 million unemployed workers and their dependents will lose their unemployment benefits on January 1.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Support for restoring improvements to the Earned Income Tax Credit and the Child Care Credit.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Support for reintroducing the 2009 Recovery Act refundable tax credit of $500 for individuals and $1,000 for families earning under $110,000 to preserve purchasing power lost by an end to the 2% FICA payroll tax cut.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Support for abolishing the Bush tax cuts on the top 2%.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Support for taxing capital gains and stock dividends at the same rate as earned income.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Support for increasing effective corporate taxation through the elimination of corporate tax loopholes and corporate “tax expenditures”.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"These reforms would yield $275 billion in additional annual revenue.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Instituting a “Robin Hood Tax” could net another $300 billion in annual revenues.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"A “Robin Hood Tax” is a small sales tax, for example 0.25%, charged on all trading in stocks, currencies and debt instruments such as bonds, derivatives, futures and options.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
